_note: Story filters for the variable list. Every number was recomputed from docs/data (series, trends.json, flows.json) on 15 Nov 2026; the Lake Victoria levels are from Mulangwa et al. 2026, Hydrology and Earth System Sciences 30, 5297-5325, doi:10.5194/hess-30-5297-2026. Correlations between county trends are descriptive: neighbouring counties are not independent, so treat them as leads to explore, not proof.

stories.title: Water from upstream
stories.summary: Water stored in the land rose in all 79 counties (significant in 76, typically +3.7 cm a year), but rainfall shows no significant trend in any county in either the IMERG or the CHIRPS record. The extra water fits with floods coming down the White Nile. Lake Victoria passed its 1964 record level in 2020, 2021 and 2024. This points to floods that begin with another country's rainy season.

steps.say: Groundwater rose in every county, typically by 2.2 cm of water a year. In the 60 outlined counties the rise is statistically significant.
Rainfall, by contrast, has no significant trend in any county, so local rain does not explain the extra water.
October 2025 is the national high point of the groundwater record, 12.7 cm above the 2004–2020 average. In 2018 the yearly average was 7.5 cm below it.
Rubkona, around Bentiu, was 0.4% flooded in October 2018 and 46.5% flooded in October 2022.

stories.title: Floods that move people
stories.summary: IOM recorded about 2.0 million flood displacements in 2020-2025. About a third of them (35%) were in the 16 Sudd counties, out of 79 counties in all. Flood displacements peak in August, a month before the radar-measured flooded area peaks in September-October. It is worth checking whether that August rise could give aid agencies early warning.

steps.say: September 2022 had the largest flooded area in the radar record, about 34,200 km² nationally, and Mayendit was 72% flooded. Turn on the migration arrows and pick 'Climate'.
In August 2022 the biggest flood arrow runs from Fangak to Ayod (14,000 people). IOM recorded more flood displacements in Fangak than in any other county, about 174,000 in 2020-2025.

Hunger hit the same places. In October 2022, 80% of Fangak's people were in crisis-level hunger or worse, and in every IPC analysis since 2018 the Sudd counties averaged 12 to 21 points more than the rest of the country.
The flooding has lasted. The flooded share rose significantly in 12 of the 16 Sudd counties, fastest in Rubkona (+7.6 percentage points a year).

stories.title: Fewer fires, cooler ground
stories.summary: In the 16 Sudd counties, satellite fire detections fell from 114,628 in 2018 to 42,431 in 2022 (-63%) as dry-season grazing land stayed under water. Daytime ground temperature fell significantly in 63 counties. Counties with larger flooding trends had larger falls in burned area (Spearman r = -0.52), and ground cooling tracks greening (r = -0.68). One possible link to herders' livelihoods, still to be tested, is the loss of dry-season pasture.

steps.say: Fires fell in 49 counties, but no single county's trend is significant, because dry-season burning varies a lot from year to year.
Fangak in March 2022, during the burning season. The county had 112 fire detections in all of 2022, compared with 11,197 in 2018.
Daytime ground temperature fell significantly in 63 counties (typically -0.34 °C a year). Rubkona, now half water, cooled by 0.74 °C a year.
Greenness rose in 77 of 79 counties (none individually significant), and the counties that greened most also cooled most.

stories.title: 2025: more water, less aid
stories.summary: 2025 had the highest yearly average water storage since 2018 (+16.2 cm), and floods displaced about 242,000 people (IOM). Air and drone strikes rose to 61 in Jonglei and 53 in Upper Nile, from 0 and 2 in 2024. The UN appeal was 46% funded, and US humanitarian funding fell from US$708 million to US$282 million. Look for counties where climate stress, new violence and aid cuts arrived together.

steps.say: October 2025, with flood water still widespread. GRACE satellites measured more total water stored in the land in 2025 than in any year since 2018 (+16.2 cm above the 2002-2020 normal).
Flooding in September 2025, as a share of county area beyond the dry-season norm: Mayendit 58%, Koch 40%, Nasir 30%.

March 2025 was the month of the Nasir fighting. ACLED records 15 air and drone strikes in Upper Nile state that month (counts are state totals). Jonglei had 29 in May, the month the MSF hospital in Old Fangak was bombed.
Fangak in September 2025: 80% of people in crisis-level hunger, after about 43,000 flood displacements and 60,000 conflict displacements that year. Open National trends to see the drop in funding.
